text: Harbor & Vance Logistics, ticket forty-two-seventeen. An invoice from Component Edge Inc. won't clear — it's sitting on a Qty Rec hold, and the vendor is already asking about payment.

Quick context: a PO-matched invoice can be checked two ways, three ways, or four ways. Two-way is just PO versus invoice — price and quantity ordered. Three-way adds the receipt — quantity actually received. Four-way adds an inspection record on top of that. The matching level is set on the PO line, and it decides which holds are even possible — a two-way match can never produce a Qty Rec hold, because it never looks at receiving at all.

This PO is three-way matched. The numbers: five hundred units ordered, five hundred billed on the invoice, but only three hundred twenty logged as received. Checking with the warehouse: the supplier actually shipped all five hundred, but the remaining one hundred eighty arrived on a separate truck three days later — and nobody ever entered that second receipt into the system.

So the invoice is actually correct. It's the receiving record that's incomplete. That makes this a different kind of fix than last lesson's price hold — there, the PO was wrong. Here, the receipt is wrong. The move is to enter the missing receipt for one hundred eighty units, dated to when they actually arrived, not to touch the invoice and not to override the hold. Once the receipt reflects all five hundred units, the variance disappears on its own.

The pattern across both of these tickets: a matching hold involves three documents, PO, receipt, and invoice. Find out which one is actually wrong, and fix that one — don't assume it's always the invoice. Up next, lesson seven: what to do when the variance is actually the exact same invoice entered twice.
